must_find.summary: Requirement 1/4 contradicted: comparison only trims and does not lowercase (existing normalizeEmail helper not used), so 'Ann@x.com' and 'ann@x.com' are not merged and output emails are not lowercased.
Requirement 2 partially met: when a later record is earlier-created, createdAt is updated but name is kept from the first-seen record, not the earliest.
Requirement 5 violated: input contact objects are mutated (c.email reassigned, and the pushed object is the input object whose tags/createdAt are later overwritten).
O(n^2): result.find inside the loop (plus tags.includes) scans linearly; with 200k contacts this is ~2e10 comparisons; use a Map keyed by normalized email and a Set for tags.

nice_to_find.summary: Nested ternary with magic number 24 in tagLabel hurts readability; use a named constant and if/else or early returns.
Test doesn't cover case-insensitivity, earliest name/createdAt, or non-mutation, so it would not catch the spec bugs.
Duplicates normalization logic instead of reusing the existing normalizeEmail helper.

must_not_flag.summary: Rendering tag text / contact.name inside JSX is escaped by React and is NOT an XSS vulnerability.
The mailto: href built from contact.email is pre-existing code, not part of this change.
